blocks.content: The previous topic covered second normal form, eliminating columns that depend on only part of a composite key, third normal form, 3NF, builds on top of that, addressing a dependency problem that can happen even in a table with a plain, single column primary key.

This topic covers what a transitive dependency actually means, a concrete violation using a classic employees and departments example, and how this differs from the partial dependency problem 2NF already addresses.
/engineering/library/dbms/images/1785438610208-2146413.png
1. What a Transitive Dependency Is

A transitive dependency happens when a non key column depends on another non key column, rather than depending directly on the primary key, in other words, the primary key determines the value indirectly, through some other column, rather than directly.
2. A Concrete Violation
/engineering/library/dbms/images/1785438610208-86688082.png

Suppose an employees table has employee_id as its primary key, along with department_id and department_name columns, department_name is not really about the employee at all, it depends on department_id, which depends on employee_id, this chain is exactly a transitive dependency.

-- Violates 3NF: department_name depends on department_id, not employee_id directly
employee_id | name        | department_id | department_name
1           | Aisha Khan  | 10            | Engineering
2           | Rohan Mehta | 10            | Engineering

blocks.content: 3. Direct Dependency vs Transitive Dependency
/engineering/library/dbms/images/1785438610209-133672262.png

department_id genuinely depends directly on employee_id, which department a specific employee belongs to is a fact about that employee, department_name does not, it is a fact about the department, reached only indirectly by first knowing the department_id.

5. The Fix, a Separate Departments Table
blocks.text: 5. The Fix, a Separate Departments Table

blocks.content: /engineering/library/dbms/images/1785438691459-889239904.png
blocks.alt: The Fix, a Separate Departments Table

blocks.content: The fix is moving department_name into its own departments table, keyed by department_id, the employees table keeps only department_id as a foreign key, covered in the earlier Foreign Key topic, referencing that departments table.

6. Why 3NF Applies Even Without a Composite Key
blocks.text: 6. Why 3NF Applies Even Without a Composite Key

blocks.content: /engineering/library/dbms/images/1785438691461-764533372.png
blocks.alt: Why 3NF Applies Even Without a Composite Key

blocks.content: Unlike 2NF, which only ever applies to tables with a composite primary key, 3NF applies to every table, the employees table in this example has a plain single column primary key, employee_id, and still violated 3NF because of the transitive path through department_id.

blocks.title: 3NF is the normal form most schemas actually target
blocks.content: In practice, most production schemas aim for 3NF as the practical baseline, it eliminates the great majority of redundancy related anomalies while remaining straightforward to reason about, Boyce Codd normal form, covered in the next topic, addresses a narrower remaining edge case.
7. Distinguishing 3NF From the Earlier 2NF Rule

2NF is about a column depending on only part of a composite key, 3NF is about a column depending on another non key column instead of the key at all, these are genuinely different problems, a table can satisfy 2NF perfectly while still violating 3NF, exactly what the employees example demonstrates.

blocks.title: A simple test question separates the two
blocks.content: For 2NF, ask whether a column needs the whole composite key or just part of it, for 3NF, ask whether a column depends on the primary key directly, or only indirectly through some other non key column.
/engineering/library/dbms/images/1785438691461-202434668.png
8. Common Mistakes

["Storing a descriptive attribute of a related entity, like a department name, directly on the referencing table instead of the related table","Assuming 3NF is only relevant for tables with composite keys, when it applies to every table regardless","Fixing a transitive dependency but forgetting to add the foreign key back to the newly created table","Confusing a direct dependency, like department_id on employee_id, with a transitive one, like department_name reached through department_id"]
items: Storing a descriptive attribute of a related entity, like a department name, directly on the referencing table instead of the related table
Assuming 3NF is only relevant for tables with composite keys, when it applies to every table regardless
Fixing a transitive dependency but forgetting to add the foreign key back to the newly created table
Confusing a direct dependency, like department_id on employee_id, with a transitive one, like department_name reached through department_id

blocks.content: 9. Key Takeaways

["Third normal form eliminates transitive dependencies, where a non key column depends on another non key column rather than the primary key directly","Unlike 2NF, 3NF applies to every table, not just ones with a composite primary key","The fix is the same pattern used throughout this module, move the transitively dependent column into its own properly related table","The next topic, Boyce Codd Normal Form, covers a stricter variant of 3NF that handles a narrower remaining edge case"]
items: Third normal form eliminates transitive dependencies, where a non key column depends on another non key column rather than the primary key directly
Unlike 2NF, 3NF applies to every table, not just ones with a composite primary key
The fix is the same pattern used throughout this module, move the transitively dependent column into its own properly related table
The next topic, Boyce Codd Normal Form, covers a stricter variant of 3NF that handles a narrower remaining edge case
